questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles. If you stop suddenly in front of a large vehicle, the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue makes you slower to make decisions and increases your crash risk. When you are tired, you could fall asleep while driving and crash, which can hurt or kill you or others.

questions.question: What can happen when you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Legal medicines, whether prescription or over-the-counter, can make it harder to drive. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, the effects of alcohol will decrease only by:

options.text: Taking a cold shower.
Waiting several hours.
Drinking several cups of coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol's effects from your body. Drinking coffee, exercising, or taking a cold shower will not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes to warn other drivers. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving your vehicle left or right.

questions.question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards when driving near a school. Watch for them and follow their directions.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone as quickly as possible.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed throughout the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone and be ready to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and hazards.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces your alertness and focus, slows your reaction time, and makes coordination much harder.

questions.question: Driving under the influence of any medication that impairs your driving is permitted:

options.text: Under no circumstances.
If you don't feel drowsy.
If it is prescribed by a physician.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that affects your driving ability. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When you take any medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it will affect your driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive more slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it will affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Legal medicines, whether prescription or over-the-counter, can affect your driving. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine will affect your ability to drive. Tell your doctor if they give you a tranquilizer or sedative.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left turn.
An upcoming stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use hand and arm signals to tell other drivers what they plan to do. A left arm straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: Which of the following substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups and cold tablets, allergy medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection. Let any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection pass first. Then proceed when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area designated for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are where pedestrians cross the street. They are often marked with white lines. Some crosswalks have no markings but are still legal crossing areas.

questions.question: The golden rule of driving is to:

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the roadway.
Drive aggressively.
Treat others the way you want to be treated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat others the way you want to be treated.
questions.explanation: The golden rule of driving is to treat other drivers the way you want to be treated. Follow traffic laws, drive responsibly, and avoid risks that could hurt you or others.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of tiredness while driving. You are too tired if you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or need the radio loud to stay awake. If this happens, park safely and rest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down to safely handle these curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve.
Drive no slower than 35 mph around the curve.
Go 35 mph or slower when entering the curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go 35 mph or slower when entering the curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming conditions. Speed advisory plaques on these signs show the safe speed for that area.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare directly in front of their car.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.
questions.explanation: A driver should watch all around their vehicle — beside, ahead, and to the rear. Know what is happening in every direction.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Look for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you about hazards.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: The safest thing to do is get out of the aggressive driver's way. Do not compete with other drivers. Always follow the rules and cooperate with other road users.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check all your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles are in the next lane.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and how fast other vehicles are going in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and how fast other vehicles are going in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as well. Your headlights only shine so far. This makes it difficult to judge how far away things are and how fast other vehicles are traveling.

questions.question: What is the rule at a crosswalk?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings. Vehicles must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked. Pedestrians must obey traffic signals.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal starts flashing. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian already in the intersection cross first. Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing before you drive.
